title: Central Bank of Chile Annual Conference: Dissented for Hike, Waiting Has a Cost
summary: Keynote at the BCCh annual conference that opens with global forces (oil, tariffs, the AI buildout and Chile's copper/lithium exposure) but closes with a full policy section explaining Cook's October dissent in favor of a further 25bp hike. She argues financial conditions are 'too accommodative', the current stance is not curtailing the AI buildout, equity prices keep supporting spending, and holding steady will widen a positive output gap; with PCE at 3.8% and core 3.2% and price increases broadening across categories, she sees 'little evidence inflation is declining.' She stresses urgency: waiting risks getting behind the curve and forcing larger hikes later, and she is 'skeptical' the single September hike will change the inflation path. Versus Oakland (Sep 28), where she backed the hike but left further steps to the data, she has moved to wanting another hike now, judges policy accommodative rather than restrictive, and frames inaction itself as a policy choice. The labor market is solid (unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +165k), so she is 'more focused on the inflation side'; AI labor risks are flagged as structural, not a reason for patience.

key_quotes.quote: I dissented from that decision. I preferred to raise the target range another 1/4 percentage point.
key_quotes.context: On the October FOMC hold, after supporting the September hike.

key_quotes.quote: First, in my view, financial conditions are too accommodative at a time when inflation remains stubbornly above target, with no clear signs of disinflation in train.
key_quotes.context: First reason for the dissent; followed by the AI buildout and equity prices supporting demand.

key_quotes.quote: Furthermore, waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve.
key_quotes.context: Second reason for the dissent: urgency, risk of upward drift in expectations.

key_quotes.quote: Still, low unemployment is consistent with achieving our maximum-employment mandate, and, therefore, as a monetary policymaker, I am more focused on the inflation side of our remit.
key_quotes.context: Labor-market section; unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +165k in October.
